children: shares fell 4.28% to $117.69 at 9:35 a.m. ET on Friday, November 6, after the drug-delivery company reported third-quarter revenue of $493 million, up 39%, and nudged up its 2026 targets. The quarter was strong. The raise looked small.

Royalty revenue, the engine of the business, rose 44% to $341 million, and GAAP diluted EPS climbed to $2.01 from $1.43. Halozyme now expects 2026 revenue of $1.860 billion to $1.925 billion, up from $1.835 billion to $1.910 billion, and non-GAAP EPS of $8.75 to $9.05 versus $8.65 to $9.00 before. That raise was smaller than investors hoped, according to Yahoo Finance.

The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 89/100, with Profitability the standout, while Financial Strength and GF Value sit mid-range. Shares trade about 14% above a GF Value of $103.65. At the midpoint, the new EPS guide puts the price near 13 times 2026 earnings, which looks modest for 39% growth; the test is whether royalties keep compounding into 2027.

title: Halozyme Stocks Slip 4.28% Despite 39% Revenue Growth and Modestly Higher Guidance
